A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, and Appendices A–D are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical results and an analytical comparison for ridge regression. Its Airfoil discussion refers to experiments from Tibshirani et al. (2019), not original empirical results.

after.justification: v2 reports original training-conditional coverage histograms for four UCI datasets in Figure 1, using Gaussian-kernel RKHS regression and 1,000 training samples.

M1.justification: The split conformal, full conformal, and weighted jackknife+ constructions in Section 2 remain unchanged. The new likelihood-ratio truncation argument changes the theoretical analysis, not the prediction procedure.

E1.justification: v2 introduces original evaluations on Wine Quality, Abalone, Concrete Compressive Strength, and Combined Cycle Power Plant, under exchangeability and artificial covariate shift. v1 contains no original dataset evaluation; its cited Airfoil example is not a removed experiment.

E2.justification: Figure 1 introduces an empirical comparison between ordinary conformal prediction under exchangeability and weighted conformal prediction under shift. v1 contains no corresponding original comparison. These methods are evaluated under different distributional conditions.

E3.justification: v2 adds one illustrative experimental protocol: 1,000 training samples, Gaussian-kernel RKHS regression, 80% target coverage, and covariate shift generated through exponential-tilt resampling. This is a new protocol, not a revision of an existing experiment.

E4.justification: Figure 1 adds a distribution-shift analysis asking how training-conditional coverage concentration differs between exchangeable and shifted settings. The existing analytical comparison of stability-based ridge-regression bounds remains.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical run counts, seeds, Monte Carlo errors, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new histograms display the coverage distribution being studied without quantifying uncertainty in its empirical estimation.

E6.justification: v2 adds original empirical coverage distributions across four datasets, showing broader distributions and heavier tails in the weighted, shifted setting. v1 has no corresponding original empirical outcomes. These are newly reported scenario results, not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: Theorem 2 and Appendix A's Lemma 4 add a tail-dependent split-conformal bound without requiring a bounded likelihood ratio or finite second moment. The revision also tightens the entropy-integral calculation from 3C to 2C and propagates this change through the existing covariate-shift bounds.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains training-conditional guarantees for weighted conformal methods. v2's abstract adds the potential application of computing more efficient prediction sets and foregrounds the relationship between distribution-shift severity and coverage-tail behavior.

C2.justification: v2 adds an interpretation linking weighting to heavier conditional-coverage tails despite marginal validity. It also qualifies the feature-conditional impossibility discussion by specifying continuous test covariates. The known-likelihood-ratio requirement and stability-related applicability limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 supplies basic implementation information for its new illustration: Gaussian-kernel RKHS regression, training sample size, target coverage, and an exponential-tilting procedure referenced to Tibshirani et al. (2019). Exact kernel and tilting parameters and code access are not supplied.

R1.justification: v2 removes the discussion and citation connecting its likelihood-ratio regimes to Ma et al. (2023), and adds Durrett (2019) to support the new truncation argument. Its principal positioning relative to weighted conformal prediction and algorithmic-stability research remains.

P1.justification: The abstract and portions of the introduction are rewritten, with limited explanatory and notation edits elsewhere. A new Section 4, 'Fully conditional conformal prediction,' contains only one introductory sentence and shifts Discussion to Section 5; the broader organization remains.

P2.justification: v2 adds a four-panel histogram figure with coverage and density axes, exchangeability/shift legends, and a dataset-and-model caption. v1 has no corresponding figure. The remaining document retains its single-column presentation with reflowed text and equations.

improvement.justification: Figure 1 improves empirical motivation, and the sharper existing bounds offer a limited theoretical refinement. However, the new Lemma 4's final bound omits an additional tail-probability term implied by its preceding decomposition. Theorem 2 also leaves the required positivity of m' unstated, and Section 4 is unfinished. These unresolved correctness and completeness issues prevent a reliable net quality judgment despite the broader content.
